IMAP Mailbox Example

Read a mailbox with gxsIMAPClient (DataReel 7.4): log in over TLS, search, list the messages newest first and save each message's text to a spool folder once.

What It Shows

The program is the 2007 IMAP client program on the DataReel 7.4 gxsIMAPClient:

  1. Connect() with implicit TLS (port 993), or --starttls (port 143, then STARTTLS), or --plain (port 143, plain text, for a server on the same host or a test only), then Login().
  2. SelectMailbox() and Search() with IMAP search criteria (ALL by default).
  3. FetchHeader() with the arrival time and the envelope's date, for each match, newest first.
  4. With --spool, FetchBody() into a file named by the arrival time and the message number; a message already in the folder is skipped, so the program can run from cron.
  5. With --debug, the session, with the password recorded as xxxxxxxx.

Nothing is changed on the server: the fetches use BODY.PEEK and do not set \Seen.

Running It

imap_fetch host port user password [--mailbox INBOX] [--search CRITERIA] [-r number]
           [--spool folder] [--debug] [--starttls | --plain] [--ca ca.pem] [--insecure]

-r prints that whole message. --ca names the CA file for a server with a private CA (the test server); --insecure skips the certificate check (tests only). The exit code is 0 when every step succeeded.

Sample Output

Against the mock server of tests/run_tests.sh, twice with the same spool folder:

How It Is Tested

tests/run_tests.sh runs it against the mock IMAP server in tests/mock_servers.py (implicit TLS, STARTTLS, plain text, 8-bit logins sent as literals, a refused password, LOGINDISABLED, a server without STARTTLS, search, the spool and the masked session) and against a local IMAP server in a container on 127.0.0.1 (tests/imap_container_check.sh), removed after the test.

Source

examples/tls/imap_fetch.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as imap_fetch and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
